notes.note: No business CRM write in this package. The lineage lists 3 script 'write components'; none of them writes business data to CRM.

Package\Extract GZ  Fiels\Extract GZ Fiels (DTSX 3412) is NOT a CRM writer: it only does file I/O. It lists *.gz files in User::DailyFilePath (GZFilesHelper.cs:39-48), decompresses each next to the source (File.Create, GZFilesHelper.cs:13-37 / DTSX 3851), copies it to <path>\Archive GZ\yyyy-MM-dd and deletes the original (File.Copy/File.Delete, GZFilesHelper.cs:49-56 / DTSX 3885). The classifier flagged File.Create/File.Delete as crm-sdk-create/delete. User::MonthlyFilePath is read-only-declared but the line that would add it is commented out (main.cs:124). Exceptions become rows on the Error output (Description = ex.Message, main.cs:133-136, 146-149, 155-159), which only feed ETL_Warning.

Package\Extract GZ  Fiels\ETL_Warning (DTSX 2535; Create gen_etlprocesswarning, code DTSX 2721-2734) and Package\End ETL Process record\ETL Record Finish (DTSX 793; Update gen_etlprocess statuscode/gen_runtime, code DTSX 1037-1046) are ETL plumbing and are not mapped. Their open script outputs (Extract GZ Fiels.Error.Description, Get gen_etlprocessid.Output 0.gen_etlprocessid) are intentionally left unresolved.

Control-flow plumbing also not mapped: Package\Create ETL Process record (Create gen_etlprocess, DTSX 513-519) and Package.EventHandlers[OnError]\Error ETL Process record (Update gen_etlprocess statuscode 277880001 + Create annotation on the gen_etlprocess with notetext = User::ErrorDescription, DTSX 5480-5495).

Raw DTSX grep for CRM writes (\.Create\(|\.Update\(|\.Delete\(|\.Execute\(|ExecuteNonQuery|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|MERGE) finds only the four plumbing writes above plus File.Create/File.Delete (DTSX 3851, 3885). Connection [psql] (ALTSHULER_MSCRM) is used only for reads (gen_etlvariable, gen_etlprocess lookup).
